picks.title: U.S. ETF BTC Holdings
picks.description: Bitcoin held by each U.S. spot bitcoin ETF, largest to smallest. BlackRock's IBIT holds far more than any other fund; Fidelity's FBTC is second at about 177,500 BTC.
picks.reason: U.S. bitcoin ETFs just logged record November outflows of over $5 billion, led by IBIT. This shows who holds the coins that are leaving.

picks.title: Bitcoin bear markets compared: decline from each cycle peak, by days since the peak
picks.description: Bitcoin's decline from each cycle peak by days since the peak: Dec 2017, Nov 2021 and the Oct 6 2025 peak ($124,753). The current drawdown sits near -37%, much shallower than the -75% to -80% troughs of past cycles at the same point.
picks.reason: Bitcoin is stuck near $60K with sentiment at multi-year lows. This puts the current bear market next to the last two.

picks.title: SpaceX valuation: private tenders → xAI merger → IPO → market
picks.description: SpaceX's valuation path from the July 2024 private tender through the xAI merger, the June 2026 IPO, the June 16 peak close, the Aug 5 low and the Oct 20 2026 close (about $1.9 trillion).
picks.reason: Tesla and SpaceX have formed board committees to negotiate a potential merger, which puts SpaceX's valuation back in focus.

picks.title: Borrowing for AI: total debt at each fiscal year end vs the latest quarter
picks.description: Total debt of Oracle, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and CoreWeave at each fiscal year end since FY2021 vs the latest quarter (June 2026). Oracle and Amazon are each near $130 billion, and Alphabet passed $100 billion.
picks.reason: The AI stock selloff has investors questioning the debt behind the data center build-out. This shows how fast that borrowing grew.

picks.title: GPU rental prices, on-demand ($/GPU-hour)
picks.description: On-demand GPU rental prices in dollars per GPU-hour for H100 SXM, H100 PCIe, H200 SXM, B200 and A100 since August 2026. B200 rents for roughly $8.50 to $9 an hour, H200 for about $6.50, and H100 SXM for about $4.
picks.reason: With AI chip stocks selling off on demand worries, rental prices are a live read on compute demand, and they are holding up or rising.
